object_description: elegant filigree five-storey structure of horizontal layers around a very large atrium
geometry_property: outer and inner ring of slender columns
design_condition: the structure completely occupies the building perimeter in a cramped situation, leaving no significant outdoor space and organising all floors around a full-height atrium

positive: An elegant and filigree five-storey structure with horizontal layering for the cramped situation
The design is characterised by generous openness, transparency and lightness
The supporting structure determines the external appearance and the functional and spatial structure
Slender alternately vertical and inclined composite columns with a few wall panels carry loads and bracing
The vertical load-bearing elements are reduced as much as possible in the interest of flexibility
The wide-span hybrid ceilings and two lateral cores give very high and future-proof flexibility on all floors
The interplay of structure and a full-height atrium with open learning zones is the real heart of the complex
At about 20 by 28 metres the atrium has impressive dimensions and is identity-forming
It is structured by the internal load-bearing layer and the school rooms arranged outside
Two additional vertical connections increase flexibility
The largely open ground floor with direct main access logically holds the cafeteria and media library
The administrative units are densely packed and concentrated on one floor
The architectural appearance is consistently derived from the primary structure
Conical concrete elements create spatial depth in the facade and partially shade the glazing
From an operational point of view the project creates very good conditions
A compact appearance of a pleasing volume
A convincing and self-confident urban and architectural statement
The structural and spatial disposition is of high quality and truly identity-creating
It forms the basic framework for efficient and flexible school operations
negative: The structure offers no significant outdoor spaces
The unconditional striving for all-pervading transparency seems a little too forced
The impressive spatial continuum places high demands on acoustics, furnishings and users
The transparency to the outside suggested by the interior images is unlikely to correspond to reality
There is no direct view to the outside and glazed internal partitions will require privacy measures
The external venetian blinds are likely to have a major impact on the facade appearance
The design of the learning islands raises a few question marks
The project has the largest floor area and largest building volume
The elaborate facade materialisation and high proportion of glass have a cost-driving effect
It has the highest construction costs in comparison
The disposition places special demands on the building design and internal use
